extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, press officers, journalists, and science-communication scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluation criteria for assessing press releases and related news coverage of two‑arm, parallel‑group randomized controlled trials (RCTs), including definitions and types of reporting 'spin', content completeness, interpretation rubrics, and analytic methods used to identify factors associated with misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'spin'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Spin' defined as specific reporting strategies (intentional or unintentional) emphasizing the beneficial effect of the experimental treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes focus on statistically significant results (within‑group comparisons, subgroup analyses, secondary outcomes, modified populations), interpreting nonstatistically significant primary outcomes as equivalence, inadequate claims of safety, or any emphasis of beneficial effect beyond what the trial supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: No acknowledgement of nonstatistically significant primary outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to acknowledge that the primary outcome(s) were not statistically significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts as a type of 'spin'; example frequency reported (20% in article abstracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming equivalence when results failed to demonstrate a statistically significant difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting a nonstatistically significant difference as showing equivalence or comparable effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorized as 'spin' (example: interpreting p>0.05 as equivalence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on positive secondary outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasizing statistically significant secondary outcomes while primary outcomes are nonstatistically significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a form of 'spin' when it shifts emphasis away from primary outcome results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on inappropriate subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlighting subgroup analyses (especially post hoc or not prespecified) to present positive findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts as 'spin' if it inappropriately promotes subgroup findings over primary outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on within‑group (or over‑all within) comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on within‑group changes rather than between‑group comparisons to suggest treatment benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a misleading emphasis; part of classification of 'spin'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatistically significant outcome reported as if it were significant
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting nonstatistically significant results in language implying statistical significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly listed as a type of 'spin' (e.g., 'nonstatistically significant outcome reported as if they were significant').

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignored data of safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Omitting or downplaying safety/adverse event data in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts as 'spin' when safety information is neglected or omitted from press releases/news items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate claim of safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Making claims of safety that the data do not support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified as 'spin' when safety is overstated without adequate evidence or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate extrapolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Extending findings beyond the population, context, or evidence supported by the trial (e.g., from animals/lab to humans or from a small trial to broad clinical practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered 'spin' and an important misreporting type; press releases should avoid extrapolation without caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of any 'spin' as a binary evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether at least one type of 'spin' is present in the abstract conclusion, press release, or news item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary outcome in analysis (e.g., 47% of press releases had at least one type of 'spin').

rubrics_metrics.name: Easy access to full article (link or full reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release provides direct link or full citation to the related scientific article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a content completeness criterion; half the press releases provided easy access. Recommended for journalists to check original source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding source reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release discloses the funding source for the study (profit, nonprofit, both, or not reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded as a characteristic; lack of reporting flagged. Not associated with 'spin' in their bivariate analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release explicitly states the study design (e.g., randomized controlled trial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of completeness checklist for press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release reports the trial sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a characteristic; small sample size (<112 in this study) was associated with higher frequency of 'spin' and overestimation of benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of follow‑up reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release indicates follow‑up duration for outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered part of essential trial information for journalists and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes clearly identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release identifies which outcomes are primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential for correct interpretation; omission may facilitate 'spin' or misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of primary outcome reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcomes reported 'adequately' defined as with effect size and precision or treatment effect in each arm with precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit standard was used to classify adequacy of reporting (table footnote); 'adequate' reporting reduces risk of misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes reported in words only vs quantitative (effect size/precision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether primary outcomes are reported only qualitatively (words) or quantitatively with effect sizes and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word‑only reporting (41% in press releases) may increase risk of misinterpretation; quantitative detail preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety reporting (mentioned vs quantified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether safety/adverse events are mentioned and whether they are quantified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases should quantify safety data where possible; omission or vague mention counts against completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study limitations reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release includes study limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 14% reported limitations in this sample; including limitations is recommended to avoid overstating findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of interviews/quotations (authors, experts) and quote tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release includes quotes from authors or editorialists, and whether the quotes emphasize or moderate the findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes can either amplify 'spin' ('this work paves the way') or introduce caution ('further investigation is needed'); quote content should be scrutinized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article quotation reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotations from the scientific article included in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used, quotations should not overstate findings; presence recorded (31% in sample) and tone evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author of press release (press officer vs other) as an evaluative variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether press releases written by press officers differ in quality or propensity for 'spin' compared to other authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded as a variable; in this study author type was not associated with 'spin' frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation scale for RCT results (1–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors rate whether patients should: 1) definitely get the experimental treatment, 2) probably get it, 3) decide for themselves (neutral), 4) probably not get it, 5) definitely not get it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping: scores 1–2 = treatment considered beneficial; 3 = neutral; 4–5 = not beneficial. Used to compare interpretations from article, press release, and news items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of misinterpretation (difference by at least one class)
rubrics_metrics.description: Misinterpretation defined as interpretation of the press release or news item differing from that based on the full‑text article by at least one class on the three‑class system (beneficial/neutral/not beneficial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misinterpretation can be overestimation or underestimation of benefit; used as analysis outcome (e.g., 31% of press releases misinterpreted results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overestimation/underestimation of benefit (directional misinterpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the press release/news overestimates (rates more beneficial) or underestimates the treatment effect compared with the article interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify and categorize misinterpretation events (e.g., most misinterpretations were overestimations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding of assessors in interpretation tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors interpreting press releases were blinded to authors, article content, and journal; assessors of news items were blinded to press release and article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding recommended to reduce bias when evaluating how press releases/news items represent trial results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized data‑abstraction form and independent review
rubrics_metrics.description: Data were abstracted via a standardized form; subjective items (like type of 'spin') abstracted by two independent reviewers with consensus; other data by single reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized forms and double abstraction for subjective items increase reliability; report inter‑rater agreement (kappa reported ~0.56).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter‑rater reliability reporting and consensus resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Report concordance and kappa for assessments of subjective items and resolve discrepancies by consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean kappa for 'spin' assessment reported (0.56); important to show reproducibility of qualitative coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for eligible press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Include press releases indexed in EurekAlert! between specified dates, topic 'medicine and health', type 'research news', keyword 'random*'; include only press releases for two‑arm, parallel‑group RCTs and exclude equivalence/noninferiority, cross‑over, cluster, multiple‑arm trials, follow‑up studies, non‑English releases, press releases about more than one study, and duplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria ensure a homogeneous, comparable sample for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis and model selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Bivariate analyses use chi‑square/Fisher exact for categorical and Student t‑test for quantitative variables; multivariable analysis via Poisson regression with robust error variance and bootstrap model selection (1,000 samples). Variables with p<0.25 in bivariate selection considered; variables retained in ≥60% of bootstrap samples kept in final model; express results as risk ratios and 95% CIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these analytic choices when assessing factors associated with 'spin' and misinterpretation; rationale documented (e.g., no multivariable model for some outcomes due to few events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: press releases should provide basic information for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release should provide journalists with the basic information needed to develop a news story and publish it in the mass media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes links to articles, contextualization of findings, contact details, and necessary caveats; press releases are not full papers but should not overstate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of exaggerated investigator quotes and overstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should avoid investigator quotes that overstate the importance or implications of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior studies cited found many quotes exaggerated; quotes should moderate claims and include caution when appropriate.
